content:
If you've been using apps on the Apple Watch beta all summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to open on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating these apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

These updates will be pushed through the App Store, with the version release notes reading: "This app was updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features."

Apple notified developers this week that the entire process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, along with iOS 27 and all the other new operating systems, is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates are being rolled out in time.

Apple said this arrangement is necessary because some watchOS apps have issues with the arm64 architecture. It is understood that they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning properly without any action required from developers.
